claims.text: The untreated nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a homogeneous, fully metallic solid-solution surface.
A controlled electrochemical potential hold or mild oxidative pretreatment will induce partial surface oxidation in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The treatment will selectively oxidize less noble Ru while leaving Pt and Ir metallic.
The treatment will produce oxidized sites adjacent to metallic Pt and Ir sites.
Selective partial oxidation will modify the local electronic structure of neighboring metallic sites.
The mixed oxidation state will adjust the adsorption energies of ethanol and its dehydrogenated intermediates.
Adjusted intermediate adsorption energies will reduce activation barriers for key ethanol-oxidation steps.
The mixed oxidation state will reduce the activation barrier for C–C bond cleavage.
Partially oxidized PtPdRhRuIrOs will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the untreated metallic baseline.
Partially oxidized PtPdRhRuIrOs will exhibit altered product selectivity relative to the untreated metallic baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies at moderate potentials and temperatures typical of ethanol oxidation.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply if the surface becomes completely oxidized.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply if catalyst dissolution occurs.
Partial oxidation has been associated with enhanced electrocatalytic activity in another high-entropy alloy system.
The exact contribution of each PtPdRhRuIrOs constituent and the optimal degree of oxidation are not established.
